checks: For t approaching an endpoint, interpolate each point of the endpoint slice with one fixed point of an interior slice to obtain the Hausdorff lower inclusion. Compactness gives the upper inclusion. The section volume is continuous even for a null endpoint section. Its nonnegative concave d-th root is absolutely continuous on the closed interval, so its bounded d-th power is too. For d=0 the profile is constant on the closed interval.

The distributional derivative of the zero extension has atoms +f(a) at a and −f(b) at b. Piecewise integration by parts gives −∫f, the positive contributions f(k) at interior integers, and B(b−)f(b)−B(a+)f(a). At noninteger endpoints the last terms cancel the atoms, and at integer endpoints the chosen B-value is zero while the one-sided terms each pay one half. The frozen proof corrects the sign order of the noninteger boundary expression in the prose of the source; its displayed source identity already has the correct sign.
As independent endpoint checks, for d=0 the interval [0,1] gives 1+1=2 sampled sites, [1/4,3/4] gives 1/2−1/2=0 sites, and [0,3/4] gives 3/4−1/4+1/2=1 site.

The divergence theorem gives the surface integral as ∫g′f=−∫g dDf. Symmetric regularization of the sawtooth converges to zero at each integer and to its value everywhere else, with a uniform bound on the compact range. Both finite signed integrals therefore converge with the stated representative.

If a lower-dimensional ambient convex set has a positive d-slice, the slice has affine dimension d and spans the affine hull of the whole set. That hull is the single fixed-base plane and contributes precisely when its base is an integer. This includes the point case d=0.

overlap.comparison: Its quadrature formula uses a continuous half-line profile with a derivative of bounded variation and estimates the trapezoidal error. The present general convex section profile can jump at support endpoints and the statement keeps exact endpoint atoms and their surface-flux expression.

Its second-order Bernoulli formula applies to the square of a continuous piecewise affine profile vanishing at support endpoints. It supplies a bound for that class, not the exact first-order formula with closed endpoints.

readability: B(b−) and B(a+) refer to the interior one-sided limits. The closed section at an integer endpoint carries its full fiber mass even though the derivative pairing assigns zero to the atom there.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact discrete quadrature identity, both closed endpoint terms, and the signed surface-flux representation have the correct signs and measures.
